title: Home Alone Director Questions Legacy Sequel as Culkin Return Emerges
excerpt:
Chris Columbus argues that a true Home Alone legacy sequel would be difficult without Catherine O'Hara.
Meanwhile, reports describe a new project involving Macaulay Culkin, Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg.
body_md:
Reports of a new Home Alone film involving Macaulay Culkin have arrived alongside strikingly skeptical comments from Chris Columbus, director of the first two movies. The timing has created an unusual contrast between the filmmaker's view of what made the original successful and the reported plans for a new installment.

Columbus argues that the franchise's emotional center was the relationship between Kevin McCallister and his mother, played by Catherine O'Hara. He described the two performers as essential to the first film's appeal. Following O'Hara's death in January 2026, he believes a genuine reunion built around that same relationship can no longer happen.

He did not completely rule out another movie involving members of the original cast. His concern was that later installments often misunderstand why a particular ensemble works. In his view, the chemistry among actors matters as much as the high-concept premise of a child defending a house against burglars.

At the same time, a report says Culkin is set to reprise Kevin in a new project, with Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg reportedly involved as writers and producers. These are reported development details rather than a complete production announcement. A release date, full cast and finalized plot have not been provided.

Columbus reportedly had no knowledge of the developing project when he gave his interview and declined further comment after learning about it. His own schedule includes preparations for Gremlins 3, which the report says is expected to begin filming in early 2027.

Culkin has previously discussed possible ways to revisit Kevin as an adult while introducing a younger generation of characters. Whether the new film follows that concept remains unclear. It is likewise unknown how the production might acknowledge O'Hara's contribution to the series.

The debate ultimately goes beyond nostalgia. A successful continuation would need to decide whether it can recreate the emotional warmth of the original without one of its defining performers, or whether a different kind of Home Alone story is the more credible path forward.
